item.title: Decarbonizing Transport via Multimodal Systems
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the critical challenge of decarbonizing transport through the development and implementation of multimodal transportation systems. Multimodal transport integration represents a key strategy for achieving substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and improving overall sustainability in the transportation sector.

Appel publié par Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Integration of multiple transport modes to reduce carbon emissions
  • Sustainable mobility solutions and transitions
  • Life cycle assessment of multimodal transport systems
  • Policy frameworks for decarbonizing transport
  • Technology and infrastructure innovations for multimodal systems
  • Behavioral and social aspects of multimodal transport adoption
  • Urban and regional planning for sustainable transport
  • Electric and alternative fuel vehicles in multimodal networks

item.title: From Vision to Practice: Realizing Net-Zero Manufacturing Through Circular Economy and Smart Production
item.content:encoded:
Yasser Dessouky, San Jose State University

Masood Fathi, University of Skövde

Taha Arbaoui, INSA Lyon

Khaled Hadj-Hamou, INSA Lyon

Ming-Lang Tseng, Asia University

This special issue addresses the critical challenge of transitioning manufacturing to net-zero operations by integrating circular economy principles with smart production technologies. The issue seeks research on how organizations can move from sustainability commitments to practical implementation strategies that reduce emissions, minimize waste, and create climate-neutral industrial systems.

The collection welcomes original research, case studies, and reviews that demonstrate emerging technologies and system-wide transformation frameworks. Topics range from Industry 4.0 applications and AI-driven optimization to supply chain decarbonization, renewable energy integration, and the role of regulatory policies in driving sustainable manufacturing practices.

Appel publié par International Journal of Production Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Closed-loop supply chains and waste reduction initiatives for low-carbon and climate-resilient manufacturing
  • Industry 4.0-enabled smart operations for net-zero manufacturing transformation
  • Life-cycle assessment of sustainable manufacturing processes
  • AI-driven optimization for energy-efficient production
  • Big data analytics and decision support for carbon footprint reduction
  • Renewable energy integration into industrial production systems
  • Electrification of industrial processes for carbon neutrality
  • AI-powered energy forecasting and optimization in manufacturing
  • The impact of carbon pricing and regulatory policies on production systems
  • Economic incentives and financial mechanisms for green manufacturing
  • Cross-sectoral collaboration for achieving net-zero industry goals
  • Policy-driven roadmaps for industrial decarbonization
  • Multi-criteria decision-making for net-zero manufacturing strategy development

  • September 30, 2026: Manuscript submission deadline

item.title: Net-Zero Pathways in Logistics, Transportation, and Supply Chain Management
item.content:encoded:
Paul Tae-Woo Lee, Zhejiang University

International organizations have implemented regulations requiring decarbonization of transportation and logistics industries. The special issue addresses net-zero emissions implementation through multimodal transport networks, where major cargo owners and stakeholders have committed to zero-emission transportation. AI and big data technologies are identified as catalysts for digital transformation and carbon reduction optimization.

The special issue aims to fill research gaps concerning net-zero pathway implementation, particularly around three key challenges: direct emissions reduction, higher capital and operating costs for green technologies, and establishing sustainable green energy supply chains. The collection seeks comprehensive and integrated approaches to enable logistics and transportation industries to achieve carbon reduction and multimodal network sustainability.

Researchers are invited to explore how AI, digitalization, new technologies, and policy mechanisms can support decarbonization. The special issue targets the research community and practitioners in transport, logistics, and supply chains to provide managerial insights and expand literature on net-zero pathways.

Appel publié par International Journal of Logistics Research and Applications. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Application of AI & big data for decarbonization
  • Green shipping and digital corridors

  • Green fuel supply chains, comprising supply, transport, and storage
  • Green energy transitions in smart cities
  • Sustainable procurement for net-zero transitions
